parts.visual:
You are hiring your first 10 employees. You interview a 'B-Player'. They are average, cheap, and available right now. You interview an 'A-Player'. They are brilliant, expensive, and demand stock options. Who do you hire?

The Rule:
1. The Steve Jobs Doctrine: A small team of A+ players can run circles around a giant team of B and C players.
2. The Physics of Hiring: A-Players only want to work with other A-Players. If you hire a single B-Player, the A-Players will get frustrated and quit. B-Players will then hire C-Players to protect their own egos.
parts.audio: Your first ten hires will define the DNA of your entire company. If you compromise on talent early on just to save money or fill a desk, you have mathematically guaranteed the death of your startup.

questions.question: A founder is exhausted. They have been trying to hire a lead engineer for 6 months without success. They finally find an 'Okay' engineer (a B-Player) who is willing to start tomorrow. What should the founder do?
options: Hire them immediately to save time.
Do not hire them. Keep the position open, even if it means the founder has to work 100 hours a week to cover the gap. Lowering your hiring standards out of exhaustion is fatal.
Hire them but pay them minimum wage.
questions.correct_answer: Do not hire them. Keep the position open, even if it means the founder has to work 100 hours a week to cover the gap. Lowering your hiring standards out of exhaustion is fatal.
questions.explanation: Desperation is the enemy of a great culture.

questions.question: Listen to the CEO explaining the 'Bozo Explosion' concept. What happens when you hire a B-Player?
questions.tts_text: A-Players hire A-Players because they are confident. B-Players hire C-Players because they are terrified of someone smarter taking their job. C-Players hire D-Players. Suddenly, your company is filled with incompetent people.
options: The Talent Death Spiral. Mediocrity breeds worse mediocrity. A single weak manager will actively prevent brilliant people from joining the company in order to protect their own status.
questions.correct_answer: The Talent Death Spiral. Mediocrity breeds worse mediocrity. A single weak manager will actively prevent brilliant people from joining the company in order to protect their own status.
questions.explanation: Mediocrity is a highly contagious corporate disease.

questions.question: How do you attract A-Players to a tiny startup when Google can pay them $500,000 a year in cash?
options: By buying them a nice laptop.
By offering Equity (Stock Options) and Autonomy. A-Players want to own a piece of the machine they are building, and they want the power to make massive decisions without bureaucratic red tape.
By promising them a short work week.
questions.correct_answer: By offering Equity (Stock Options) and Autonomy. A-Players want to own a piece of the machine they are building, and they want the power to make massive decisions without bureaucratic red tape.
questions.explanation: You cannot compete with Google on cash. You compete on upside and freedom.

questions.question: What is the psychological difference between an A-Player and a B-Player when confronted with a massive, impossible problem?
options: A B-Player will wait for the founder to tell them exactly how to fix it. An A-Player will figure out how to fix it on their own, execute the solution, and then tell the founder it is done.
questions.correct_answer: A B-Player will wait for the founder to tell them exactly how to fix it. An A-Player will figure out how to fix it on their own, execute the solution, and then tell the founder it is done.

pairs.match: An elite employee who is self-motivated, highly skilled, and drives massive results
The rapid decline of company talent when B-Players are allowed to hire C-Players
The freedom to make decisions and execute work without micromanagement
Paying employees with ownership in the company rather than just cash
